texts.preamble: Sri Hasmukh Mewada, Quality Manager For ... vs The State Of A.P., Rep. By Its Through ... on 28 November, 2018 Smt Justice T. Rajani Criminal Petition No.13121 of 2011 Order:
texts.facts: This criminal petition is filed, seeking for quash of the proceedings in C.C.No.128 of 2010, against the petitioner, who is A4, on the file of the Special Judicial First Class Magistrate for Railways, Nellore. The offence alleged is under Sections 2(ia)(a)(m) read with 7(1) and Section 17(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (for short 'the Act'). 2. Heard the counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor, appearing for the respondent. 3. The case of the prosecution is that the inspection of the shop of A1 was conducted on 12.03.2009 and suspecting the quality of Mirinda Orange flavour sweetened carbonated sealed Rexiam cans to be adulterated, the inspecting officer purchased nine sealed cans, which was divided into three parts and one sample was sent to FSL for analysis on 13.03.2009. The public analyst gave his report on 20.04.2009 and the complaint was filed on 30.08.2010. Section 13(2) notice was admittedly sent on 03.08.2011 by which date the shelf life of the sample expired long back. Hence, by the date of fling of the complaint itself, the shelf life of the sample expired.
texts.arguments: 4. The counsel for the petitioner expressed that there is prejudice caused to the petitioner and by virtue of the delay caused in filing the report and issuing statutory notice, the opportunity provided under Section 13(2) of the Act to send a sample for second analysis is lost. Learned counsel also relies on an order in CRLP.Nos.2184 of 2009 and batch dated 29.06.2009 and CRLP.No.8407 of 2012 dated 25.11.2014 wherein the Court by considering the similar submissions and by taking into consideration the inordinate delay, not only in issuing notice, but also in launching prosecution against the accused, [LEAKAGE_MASK] the further proceeding. This Court in R. HARI HARA REDDY v. STATE OF ANDHRA PRADESH1 held that the inordinate delay in filing the complaint would deprive the valuable right offered on the accused under Section 13(2) of the Act. The decision of the Supreme Court in STATE OF HARYANA v. UNIQUE FARMAID (P) LTD.2 is also on the same lines. Relevant portion at paragraphs 11 and 12 observed as follows: "11. Sub-section (1) of Section 30 which appears to be relevant only prescribes in effect that ignorance would be of no defence but that does not mean that if there are contraventions of other mandatory provisions of the Act, the accused have no remedy. In State of Punjab v. National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd. [(1996) 11 SCC 613] this Court in somewhat similar circumstances said that the procedure laid down under Section 24 of the Act deprived the accused to have sample tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory and adduce evidence of the report so given in his defence. In this connection reference be made to decisions of this Court in State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal [(1998) 5 SCC 343] under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970]; Chetumal v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Anr. [(1981) 3 SCC 72} and Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf, [(1999)] 2 SCC 400] all under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Under sub-section (3) of Section 24 report signed by the Sri Hasmukh Mewada, Quality Manager For ... vs The State Of A.P., Rep.
